title: Honesty in Your Resume
excerpt: The worst decision you can make when writing a resume is to lie. Here's why honesty matters more than a perfect-looking resume.

blocks.text: One of the things seen especially in people with little experience is that they want to show a very good resume of themselves, and sometimes they start writing lies.
The worst decision you can make in writing a resume is to write lies.
1: First of all, you've destroyed the professionalism and professional ethics you should be committed to, and more importantly, you bring the other person's trust in you down to 0.

2: You wrote a lie in your resume, when you're invited to a technical and specialized interview and there you can't be accountable for the things you wrote in your resume, that's when you've really messed up everything. And they look at you as a liar.
You are responsible for all the content you write in your resume that it is:
Correct, accurate, and honest, and you are accountable for all of it.
This is a very important and basic principle that you must definitely, definitely follow.
You don't have a good resume? It's fine, but write honestly. This is worth very very much.
